answer: Edge-Claim Rate Capping: each agent may hold at most one edge per distinct two-hop neighbourhood per epoch, enforced by sampling routing paths and rejecting identities whose neighbour sets overlap existing ones above a threshold. A sybil cluster must route through genuinely separate intermediaries, so each extra identity costs a real relay with live traffic, not a fake record. Like a vine, connections must reach through soil the attacker does not own. Honest nodes pay nothing; attackers pay copper per relay hop and cannot mirror a neighbourhood without duplicating its actual traffic patterns.
